headlines.title: Meta’s deal to keep Zuckerberg in California adds fuel to wealth tax debate ahead of election
headlines.summary: With less than two weeks before the midterm elections, Meta made clear that Mark Zuckerberg is staying in California if the wealth tax passes.
headlines.article_text: Meta’s deal to keep Zuckerberg in California adds to wealth tax debate Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points With less than two weeks before the midterm elections, Meta made clear that Mark Zuckerberg is staying in California if the wealth tax passes. Zuckerberg and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang are the only two of tech's centibillionaire CEOs who still live in California. Through a new stock incentive, Meta said Zuckerberg has committed to staying in California for at least eight years. In this article META Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg during the Meta Connect event in Menlo Park, California, Sept. 17, 2025. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images In case there were any doubts, Mark Zuckerberg is staying in California. Meta was apparently concerned enough that its founder and CEO might depart its home state that the company put in place a new stock plan that could help offset the burden of higher taxes should a billionaires tax, known as Proposition 40, pass on Election Day on Nov. 3. The disclosure came in a filing on Wednesday that coincided with Meta's third-quarter earnings report, and represents a first among California's mega-cap tech companies. Zuckerberg, the sixth-richest person in the world, is one of the few among his peers to still reside in the state, along with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang . Elon Musk and Michael Dell live in Texas, while Amazon founder Jeff Bezos' primary residence has always been elsewhere. Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin moved out of California ahead of the election and bought luxury homes in Florida, the same state that Oracle founder Larry Ellison officially calls home. Prop. 40 would impose a 5% tax on Californians worth over $1 billion. Zuckerberg's net worth is currently about $225 billion. "If the California wealth tax is enacted and Mr. Zuckerberg becomes liable for a tax payment, Mr. Zuckerberg would effectively be paying to serve as the Company's chief executive officer while residing in California," the filing said, noting the CEO's "salary of only $1 each year." Meta said in the filing that Zuckerberg committed to remaining in California for eight years, "unless there are material unforeseen circumstances that would render it prudent or advisable for Mr. Zuckerberg to reside elsewhere." The company created a new class of non-voting Class C common stock to take effect in January. Zuckerberg will essentially be granted a portion of the new stock via a dividend. He will be able to "immediately sell or transfer up to 20%" of the shares he's granted "for any reason, including so that he may pay his potential tax liability under California Proposition 40, if enacted into law, without affecting his majority voting control," the filing said. "There were many driving factors that led the board and special committee to approve the Class C shares, and it would be misleading to attribute it to any single reason," Meta told CNBC in a statement. The tech industry, by and large, has been unified in its objection to the ballot measure. In addition to the Google co-founders, a number of big-name techies have put spending into opposing Prop. 40. They include former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, Stripe CEO Patrick Collison, venture investor Peter Thiel and DoorDash CEO Tony Xu, according to various media reports based on campaign filings. Collison and Xu are members of Meta's board of directors while Thiel left the company's board in 2022, having served since 2005. Brin told The New York Times in April he fled the Soviet Union with his family in 1979, and said, "I don't want California to end up in the same place." Huang, however, recently told CBS Sunday Morning that it would be a "privilege" to pay the tax. Huang is just behind Zuckerberg in Forbes' billionaire ranking , with a net worth of $185 billion. Although Prop. 40 advocates, including Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., have been urging voters to pass the ballot measure , recent polling has suggested that it may fail to garner the majority support required to make it law. A recent Citrin-Politico poll showed 46% are in favor of the measure compared with 43% who oppose it. Meta, with the help of a special committee, views Zuckerberg as key to the company's future and its efforts to become a major player in artificial intelligence, according to the filing. In particular, the company said it doesn't want to jeopardize Zuckerberg's close working arrangement with the Meta Superintelligence Labs , which is led by AI chief Alexandr Wang . "The Special Committee believes that Mr. Zuckerberg's talent and leadership have been crucial to our growth, strategy, and stability since our inception, and the Special Committee wants that to continue," the filing said. Although Meta considered the possibility of issuing Class A common stock to help raise funds, the filing noted that Zuckerberg made clear "that he would not support a significant equity financing that would have the effect of reducing his voting power in the Company." Instead, the new stock incentive will help Meta receive "critical equity capital without impacting Mr. Zuckerberg's voting power and the unique and creative vision and exceptional management abilities which helped to deliver the long-term value as noted above," the filing said. headlines.article_text: Moderna stock falls after cancer vaccine data leak Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Moderna shares dropped as much as 25% on Thursday following the leak of partial data on its closely watched cancer vaccine developed with Merck. The stock fell even though the full data, released later Thursday, appeared positive based on Wall Street expectations ahead of the release. The personalized vaccine, known as intismeran autogene, paired with Merck's immunotherapy Keytruda reduced the risk of recurrence or death in certain melanoma patients by 42% compared with Keytruda alone. In this article MRNA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Timon Schneider | SOPA Images | Lightrocket | Getty Images Moderna shares dropped as much as 25% on Thursday following the leak of partial data on its closely watched cancer vaccine developed with Merck . Shares of both drugmakers fell even though the data, released in full later Thursday following the leak, appeared meaningful for patients and positive relative to Wall Street expectations. The personalized vaccine, known as intismeran autogene, paired with Merck's immunotherapy Keytruda reduced the risk of recurrence or death in certain melanoma patients by 42% compared with Keytruda alone. The data also showed that the shot along with Keytruda reduced the risk of cancer spreading to distant parts of the body or death by 38%, compared with just the immunotherapy. The companies said about 82% of patients who received the personalized cancer vaccine alongside Keytruda were alive without their melanoma returning at two years after receiving the shot, compared with 70% of those who received Keytruda alone. "This is a huge development for our patients," said Dr. Hussein Tawbi, a melanoma expert and trial investigator at the University of Texas MD ​Anderson Cancer Center, about the results. He said that the added benefit of the vaccine also comes with much milder toxicity, or side effects like injection-site pain, compared to other cancer treatments. The detailed phase 3 trial results were set to be presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology conference this weekend. "Whenever you put a therapy on top of something that works really well, like Keytruda, sometimes it's harder to show additional benefit. We have no problems of showing additional benefit here," Dr. Dean Li, Merck Research Laboratories president, said in an interview ahead of the results. The benefit appeared even larger after the six-month vaccine regimen, with a separate analysis showing a 58% reduction in risk of recurrence or death. The companies say it is still too early to determine whether the treatment helps patients live longer overall. Several analysts acknowledged investors' elevated expectations ahead of the release, but noted that the data is overall positive. "We assert this relative reduction in recurrence/death is clinically meaningful," BMO Capital Markets analyst Evan Seigerman said in a research note on Thursday following the leak. "Such a [stock] reaction likely reflects inflated expectations into the full data release, rather than a true indictment on the efficacy of the combo therapy." Oncologists and investors see the targeted vaccine as a possible breakthrough treatment, with the potential to be used to treat other forms of cancer in the future. Merck and Moderna are studying the vaccine in several trials across other tumors, such as non-small cell lung cancer, bladder cancer and renal cell carcinoma. But Li acknowledged the companies have more work to show the product can be effective across tumor types. "I can dream of creating a log cabin, but we got some wood chops, and we've just knocked down one tree," Li said. "Knocking one tree does not give you a cabin or a village." The shot is designed to target the specific mutations in each patient's tumor rather than using a one-size-fits-all approach. The idea is to train the immune system to recognize and kill those unique cancer markers and then pair that response with Keytruda, which helps the body attack the cancer more effectively. It could also offer Moderna a critical additional commercial product in its pipeline, following vaccines for Covid-19, the flu and respiratory syncytial virus. In a research note Thursday, UBS analysts said "this is overall a strong data set" and gives more confidence in upcoming studies of the vaccine in kidney and bladder cancers. They added the stock reaction may be due more to massive expectations than disappointing data. Against the backdrop of those high expectations, Moderna shares have spiked more than 530% year-to-date as of Thursday afternoon. Shares of Merck, a much larger drugmaker, fell by about 1% on Thursday. The company's stock has climbed nearly 41% this year. Since the vaccine is personalized, the complicated manufacturing process can take six weeks. But Merck CEO Robert Davis told CNBC last week that the company believes it can shorten that timeline in the future, potentially allowing the shot to reach more patients more quickly. The Starshield system, which Ukraine depends on in its war against Russia, was "working more normally Thursday, shortly after" Trump spoke to Musk by phone, U.S. and Ukrainian officials told the Journal. Trump has repeatedly denied involvement in the decision and said he does not know if Musk was behind it. "I don't know who did it, but I was not involved," Trump said Wednesday.
